facts.text: Togiak grew from two earlier Inuit villages, Togiagamute and Togiak Station, making it the successor community of those historic settlements.
In the early 1900s, residents moved from the eastern side of Togiak Bay to the western shore because heavy winter snows made wood gathering difficult.
A 1964 flood forced some Togiak residents to establish Twin Hills, a new community northeast of the original Togiagamute site.
Togiak sits at the head of Togiak Bay, about 67 miles west of Dillingham in Alaska's Bristol Bay region.
The town lies inside Togiak National Wildlife Refuge and serves as the gateway to Walrus Island Game Sanctuary.
Archaeological evidence shows Yup'ik people inhabited the Togiak area continuously from around AD 1200 until the late 19th‑century relocations.
